# Josie Pye

- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_

## Appearance

_Not yet known._

## Personality

Josie Pye is known for her disagreeable nature and sharp tongue, which often impacts her popularity despite her specific talents. She possesses a natural aptitude for walking board fences and demonstrates skill in needlework, having won a first prize for knitted lace. Pursuing higher education purely for its own sake, she plans to attend college without the necessity of earning a livelihood.

## History

Josie Pye possessed a natural talent for walking board fences and won first prize for knitted lace at the [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition). At a party, she dared [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) to walk the ridgepole of the [Barry](../character/barry.md) kitchen roof, resulting in [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) falling and breaking her ankle.

## Quotes

> “Oh, that reminds me,” said Josie, “Queen’s is to get one of the Avery scholarships after all. The word came today. Frank Stockley told me—his uncle is one of the board of governors, you know. It will be announced in the Academy tomorrow.”
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXXIV. A Queen’s Girl P24](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0024)

> "If I don’t pass this year I’m coming back next. My father can afford to send me. Anne, Frank Stockley says that Professor Tremaine said Gilbert Blythe was sure to get the medal and that Emily Clay would likely win the Avery scholarship."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P14](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0014)

> "I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry’s kitchen roof."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)

> "I don’t believe anybody could walk a ridgepole. You couldn’t, anyhow."
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)

> "Are you going to be back next year, Miss Stacy?"
>
> — Josie Pye — [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P30](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0030)
